extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations, corporate communications, and crisis management
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study framework for analyzing and producing corporate crisis communications (including press statements, internal messaging, social media management, and policy responses) following a high-visibility incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and accurate communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues concerning ... timely and accurate communications were brought to the forefront of public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond quickly with factual information. The case notes that timeliness matters for public perception; slow responses allow negative narratives to spread. Example anti-pattern: delayed responses that let misinformation or viral footage drive the story before the organization provides context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincere apology and acceptance of responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Munoz released another statement, this time apologizing, taking full responsibility for the incident, and committing to make it right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies should appear sincere and take responsibility. The case contrasts initial language that seemed to blame the passenger (leaked staff memo) with later statements that 'took full responsibility' — the former worsened public outrage and the latter helped begin repair. Note: perceived insincerity (or slow/superficial apologies) damages recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate character, core purpose, and shared values
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate character: the enterprise’s unique identity, its differentiating purpose, mission and values; United’s Core Purpose and Shared Values are described as guiding day-to-day operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis communications should align with and reflect the organization's stated values and core purpose. Establishing and communicating shared values before crises helps guide employee and public responses. Use value statements as benchmarks for assessing whether responses are consistent with corporate character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong internal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong internal communications gives a brand the ability to create lasting relationships with its stakeholders; establishing an effective line of communication reaching all employees is especially challenging for airlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rapid, clear communication to employees (not just external audiences). The case shows internal missteps (leaked memo, communications reporting to HR) exacerbated the crisis. Best practice: direct lines between communications and senior leadership; timely staff briefings; prevent contradictory internal messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder empowerment and social-media preparedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media gives stakeholders a new level of empowerment ... making organizational issues very public. This underlines the importance of fostering strong consumer advocacy on social media even before crises occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor social platforms continuously, build positive communities before incidents, and plan for rapid engagement. Anti-pattern: ignoring or downplaying social conversations; failure to anticipate viral video/photo dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputation measurement (brand/reputation indices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation Institute defines reputation as an 'emotional bond' ... Reputation Institute gave the U.S. airline industry a rating ... and ranked United in the lowest tier of the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established reputation metrics (e.g., RepTrak, Reputation Institute scores, brand value rankings) to quantify reputation baseline and post-crisis changes. Employ these indices to prioritize remedial efforts and track recovery over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media analytics: volume, sentiment, emotions, hashtags, platform distribution, influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Over 75 percent of the related online conversation since April 10 was on Twitter ... most of the conversation holding a negative sentiment. The most popular emotions were disgust and anger. Top trending hashtags and influential users are enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure volume (posts), sentiment change (% negative/positive), predominant emotions, trending hashtags, platform share (e.g., percent on Twitter), and influencer impact. Use these analytics to target responses and assess whether sentiment is improving. Example metrics in case: 2 million posts on April 10; 22% increase in negativity; 75% of conversation on Twitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and misinformation management
rubrics_metrics.description: News media expressed an array of facts and opinions ... some media outlets misidentified Dao ... these 'sloppy' reports rapidly spread ... 'fake news' sparked a widespread initial concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively engage news outlets to provide accurate information and correct misreporting quickly. Prepare press materials, fact sheets, and spokesperson availability to reduce spread of inaccuracies. Monitor major outlets and social amplification of erroneous reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete policy changes and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: United announced three new goals centered around customer service and company culture that inspire ten policy changes ... raised the compensation cap ... require flight crews to be booked into a flight at least 60 minutes prior ... no passengers who have been seated on a flight would be asked to give up their seat except for safety or security reasons ... automated program to indicate willingness to give up seat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective crisis response includes concrete, visible policy reforms and operational changes. Publicize specific, verifiable actions (policy updates, system changes, new programs) and timelines for implementation to rebuild trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with government and regulatory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Munoz and United Airlines’ president ... appear on capitol hill before the U.S. House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee ... Kirby meets with a Senate subcommittee ... the USDOT concluded United did not violate Dao’s civil rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for governmental inquiries and hearings, provide transparent factual records, and coordinate legal and communications responses. Recognize regulatory outcomes (findings, fines, policy directives) as part of reputational remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-performance metrics as crisis indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: United’s shares were down by six percent, indicating a $1.4 billion loss in market value ... reported a $250 million loss in revenue ... decreases in passenger numbers and load factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track immediate financial indicators (stock price change, market capitalization loss, revenue impact, passenger load) to quantify business impact and to inform internal stakeholders and investors. Use these metrics to prioritize business vs. reputational responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry benchmarking (overbooking and bumping rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2016 analysis ... showed that United ranked fourth for greatest number of passenger complaints ... Figure indicates that United was right in the middle in regards to the number of passengers bumped compared to other U.S. airlines. Industry bumping rate dropped from 0.62 to 0.44 per 10,000 passengers in 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare organization performance against industry norms (bumping rates, complaint rates, compensation practices). Benchmarking highlights whether incident is systemic or outlier and helps craft appropriate policy reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis timeline and event documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline: Flight Map of United’s Crisis ... April 9: Dao is recorded ... April 10: CEO makes first official statement ... subsequent dates record statements, hearings, policy changes, and investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a detailed timeline of events, public statements, internal communications, and actions taken. Use the timeline to coordinate messaging, demonstrate responsiveness, and for post-crisis analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational reporting structure for communications leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: United’s corporate communications department ... prior to June 2017 reported to the human relations department who then reported to Munoz ... On June 15, United announced a new position that would establish a direct line of communication between the airline’s corporate communications department and United’s CEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize communications leadership with clear, senior-level access (reporting directly to CEO) to speed decision-making and ensure message alignment. Anti-pattern: communications siloed under HR or without executive access, which can delay or distort responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee sentiment and internal reputation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Glassdoor announces that Munoz maintained his above-average approval rating by his employees ... report showed a 91 percent approval rating for Munoz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor employee sentiment (surveys, Glassdoor ratings, internal feedback). Strong internal support can mitigate external reputational harm; conversely, employee disaffection can prolong crises. Incorporate employee-facing communications as part of response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training programs and measurement of customer-commitment performance
rubrics_metrics.description: United Customer Commitment explains our policies ... We have detailed training programs and system enhancements to support our employees in meeting these commitments, and we measure how well we meet them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in training and system enhancements that are defensible in crisis (documented training, measurable performance indicators). Track compliance and improvement over time and cite these when communicating reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with legal/procedural requirements for involuntary bumping
rubrics_metrics.description: The USDOT requires flights with over 30 passengers originating in the U.S. to seek volunteers prior to involuntarily bumping passengers ... federal law also mandates how much and when airlines are required to compensate passengers who are involuntarily removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow regulatory procedures (volunteer solicitation, selection criteria, mandated compensation) and communicate those procedures clearly to the public to demonstrate legal compliance. Transparency about selection procedures (how passengers are chosen) can reduce perceptions of unfairness.
